Data Structures & Algorithms.fact: Accessing an array element by a known index uses direct address calculation.
distractors: Array indexed access is O(log n).
Array indexed access is O(n).
Array indexed access is O(n log n).

Data Structures & Algorithms.fact: A stack removes the most recently inserted item first.
distractors: A stack follows FIFO order.
A stack always removes the smallest item first.
A stack always removes the largest item first.

Data Structures & Algorithms.fact: With a good hash function and controlled load factor, hash-table lookup is constant time on average, but collisions can degrade the worst case.
Data Structures & Algorithms.correct_answer: Hash-table lookup is O(1) on average and can degrade to O(n) in the worst case.
distractors: Hash-table lookup is always O(1).
Hash-table lookup is always O(log n).
Hash-table lookup is O(n log n) on average.

Data Structures & Algorithms.fact: A binary heap supports insertion and removal of the root by restoring heap order along a root-to-leaf path.
Data Structures & Algorithms.correct_answer: Insertion and extract-min/extract-max are O(log n) in a binary heap.
distractors: Both operations are O(1) in a binary heap.
Both operations are O(n) in a binary heap.
Both operations are O(n log n) in a binary heap.

Data Structures & Algorithms.fact: Standard Dijkstra's algorithm assumes edge weights are non-negative because settled shortest distances must not later decrease.
Data Structures & Algorithms.correct_answer: Standard Dijkstra's algorithm requires non-negative edge weights.
distractors: Standard Dijkstra's algorithm requires every edge weight to be exactly one.
Standard Dijkstra's algorithm works correctly with arbitrary negative cycles.
Standard Dijkstra's algorithm requires the graph to be a tree.

Data Structures & Algorithms.fact: A dynamic array occasionally performs an O(n) resize, but geometric growth spreads that cost across many appends.
Data Structures & Algorithms.correct_answer: Appending to a geometrically growing dynamic array is O(1) amortized.
distractors: Every append to a dynamic array is O(n).
Appending is O(log n) amortized.
Appending is O(n log n) amortized.

Object-Oriented Programming.fact: Encapsulation bundles state with behavior and restricts direct access to internal representation.
Object-Oriented Programming.correct_answer: Encapsulation hides internal state behind a controlled interface.
distractors: Encapsulation requires every method to be static.
Encapsulation means a class may never contain fields.
Encapsulation is the same as multiple inheritance.

Object-Oriented Programming.fact: An overriding method in a subclass supplies a new implementation for an inherited method with a compatible signature.
Object-Oriented Programming.correct_answer: Method overriding enables runtime polymorphic behavior.
distractors: Method overriding can occur only between unrelated classes.
Method overriding is identical to constructor overloading.
Method overriding prevents dynamic dispatch.

Object-Oriented Programming.fact: Composition models a has-a relationship and lets an object delegate work to contained collaborators.
Object-Oriented Programming.correct_answer: Composition represents a has-a relationship and can reduce inheritance coupling.
distractors: Composition always represents an is-a relationship.
Composition requires global variables for collaboration.
Composition prevents objects from delegating behavior.

Object-Oriented Programming.fact: An interface specifies a behavioral contract while allowing different implementations to satisfy that contract.
Object-Oriented Programming.correct_answer: An interface defines a contract that multiple implementations can satisfy.
distractors: An interface must store all application state.
An interface guarantees only one concrete implementation can exist.
An interface disables polymorphism.

Object-Oriented Programming.fact: Subtypes should be usable wherever their base type is expected without violating the behavior clients rely on.
Object-Oriented Programming.correct_answer: A subtype should preserve the behavioral expectations of its base type.
distractors: A subtype should expose fewer valid operations than its base type requires.
A subtype should deliberately break base-type invariants.
A subtype must duplicate every line of base-class code.

Object-Oriented Programming.fact: High-level policy should depend on abstractions rather than concrete low-level details, and low-level details should implement those abstractions.
Object-Oriented Programming.correct_answer: Dependency inversion makes high-level modules depend on abstractions rather than concrete implementations.
distractors: Dependency inversion requires high-level modules to instantiate every dependency directly.
Dependency inversion eliminates the need for interfaces or abstractions.
Dependency inversion means low-level modules must depend on UI code.

Operating Systems.fact: Threads in the same process normally share the process address space, while separate processes normally have separate address spaces.
Operating Systems.correct_answer: Threads in one process typically share an address space.
distractors: Every thread has a completely separate process address space.
Separate processes always share all memory automatically.
Threads cannot share code or heap memory.

Operating Systems.fact: Virtual memory gives processes virtual address spaces and allows pages to be mapped to physical memory or backing storage.
Operating Systems.correct_answer: Virtual memory maps virtual addresses to physical memory and can use secondary storage as backing.
distractors: Virtual memory means every virtual address is permanently stored only in CPU registers.
Virtual memory removes the need for address translation.
Virtual memory requires every process to use identical physical addresses.

Operating Systems.fact: A page fault occurs when a referenced virtual page is not currently mapped as present and the OS must handle the fault, often loading the page.
Operating Systems.correct_answer: A page fault transfers control to the OS because the referenced page is not currently available as required.
distractors: A page fault means the CPU arithmetic unit produced a wrong result.
A page fault occurs on every successful cache hit.
A page fault is another name for a network packet drop.

Operating Systems.fact: A mutex is used to ensure only one thread or process enters a protected critical section at a time.
Operating Systems.correct_answer: A mutex protects a critical section through mutual exclusion.
distractors: A mutex guarantees every thread executes simultaneously.
A mutex permanently disables context switching.
A mutex is used only for disk formatting.

Operating Systems.fact: The Coffman conditions for deadlock are mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no preemption, and circular wait.
Operating Systems.correct_answer: Deadlock requires mutual exclusion, hold-and-wait, no preemption, and circular wait to all hold simultaneously.
distractors: Deadlock requires only high CPU utilization.
Deadlock requires every process to terminate normally.
Deadlock is possible only when circular wait is impossible.

Operating Systems.fact: Thrashing occurs when a system spends excessive time paging because active working sets do not fit effectively in available memory.
Operating Systems.correct_answer: Thrashing is excessive paging caused by insufficient effective memory for active working sets.
distractors: Thrashing is a CPU instruction that clears all page tables.
Thrashing means the disk has no file system.
Thrashing occurs only when there are zero page faults.

DBMS.fact: A primary key identifies each row uniquely and cannot contain NULL values.
DBMS.correct_answer: A primary key uniquely identifies a row and is non-NULL.
distractors: A primary key may identify many duplicate rows intentionally.
A primary key must always contain NULL.
A table can use a primary key only for sorting, not identification.

DBMS.fact: Atomicity means a transaction is treated as an indivisible unit: either all of its operations take effect or none do.
DBMS.correct_answer: Atomicity means a transaction commits completely or has no effect.
distractors: Atomicity means every transaction must run at the same time.
Atomicity means data can never be rolled back.
Atomicity is the property that every query must use an index.

DBMS.fact: Indexes can accelerate supported reads but consume storage and add maintenance work to inserts, updates, and deletes.
DBMS.correct_answer: Indexes can improve reads while adding storage and write-maintenance overhead.
distractors: Indexes always make every write faster with no additional cost.
Indexes store no additional data structures.
Indexes can be used only on tables with one row.

DBMS.fact: Third Normal Form removes transitive dependencies of non-key attributes on candidate keys, subject to the formal 3NF condition.
DBMS.correct_answer: 3NF is intended to remove problematic transitive dependencies involving non-key attributes.
distractors: 3NF requires placing every attribute in a separate database.
3NF means every table must contain duplicate rows.
3NF intentionally adds transitive dependencies to non-key attributes.

DBMS.fact: Serializable isolation aims to make concurrent transactions behave as though they executed in some serial order.
DBMS.correct_answer: Serializable isolation provides behavior equivalent to some serial execution order.
distractors: Serializable isolation guarantees every transaction literally runs on a different database server.
Serializable isolation permits every anomaly by definition.
Serializable isolation means transactions cannot read data.

DBMS.fact: Multi-Version Concurrency Control maintains multiple row versions so readers can often observe a consistent snapshot without blocking writers in the same way as coarse locking.
DBMS.correct_answer: MVCC uses multiple data versions to support snapshot-style concurrent access.
distractors: MVCC stores exactly one version of every row at all times.
MVCC requires all readers to block all writers.
MVCC is a network routing protocol.

Computer Networks.fact: TCP provides a connection-oriented reliable ordered byte stream, while UDP is connectionless and does not provide those delivery guarantees.
Computer Networks.correct_answer: TCP provides reliable ordered delivery; UDP does not guarantee reliable ordered delivery.
distractors: UDP guarantees reliable ordered delivery while TCP never does.
TCP and UDP both guarantee identical delivery semantics.
Neither TCP nor UDP operates at the transport layer.

Computer Networks.fact: DNS resolves human-readable domain names to records such as IP addresses.
Computer Networks.correct_answer: DNS resolves domain names to records such as IP addresses.
distractors: DNS encrypts every application payload by itself.
DNS is used only to allocate CPU time slices.
DNS replaces Ethernet framing on a LAN.

Computer Networks.fact: A normal TCP connection is established using SYN, SYN-ACK, and ACK messages.
Computer Networks.correct_answer: TCP connection establishment normally uses SYN, SYN-ACK, then ACK.
distractors: TCP normally starts with ACK, ACK, ACK only.
TCP connection establishment requires a DNS zone transfer.
TCP establishes a connection using only an ICMP echo request.

Computer Networks.fact: TLS provides cryptographic protection for application traffic, including confidentiality and integrity, and normally authenticates the server using certificates.
Computer Networks.correct_answer: TLS protects application traffic with encryption and integrity checks and commonly authenticates the server.
distractors: TLS is a database normalization algorithm.
TLS guarantees that every network packet follows the same physical route.
TLS replaces IP addressing with MAC addresses.

Computer Networks.fact: Network Address Translation rewrites address and often port information so multiple private hosts can communicate through public addressing.
Computer Networks.correct_answer: NAT translates address information, often allowing multiple private hosts to share public addressing.
distractors: NAT guarantees end-to-end encryption by itself.
NAT is a CPU scheduling policy.
NAT removes the need for IP addresses on hosts.

Computer Networks.fact: CIDR uses variable-length network prefixes such as /24 or /20 to represent IP address blocks and enable route aggregation.
Computer Networks.correct_answer: CIDR represents networks with variable-length prefixes and supports route aggregation.
distractors: CIDR requires every network prefix to be /32.
CIDR is used only for encrypting DNS responses.
CIDR prevents routers from aggregating routes.

System Design.fact: A load balancer distributes incoming requests across multiple backend instances.
System Design.correct_answer: A load balancer distributes traffic across backend instances.
distractors: A load balancer stores every database row permanently.
A load balancer is used only to compile source code.
A load balancer requires all requests to go to one server.

System Design.fact: A cache keeps frequently or recently used data closer to the consumer to reduce repeated expensive retrieval or computation.
System Design.correct_answer: Caching can reduce latency and backend load for reusable data.
distractors: Caching guarantees data can never become stale.
Caching always increases database queries.
Caching is the same as deleting persistent storage.

System Design.fact: A message queue can decouple producers from consumers and absorb bursts by allowing work to be processed asynchronously.
System Design.correct_answer: A message queue decouples producers and consumers and supports asynchronous processing.
distractors: A message queue requires the producer and consumer to execute in the same process at the same instant.
A message queue eliminates every possibility of duplicate delivery automatically.
A message queue can be used only for image files.

System Design.fact: Replication keeps copies of data on multiple nodes, while sharding partitions different subsets of data across nodes.
System Design.correct_answer: Replication copies data; sharding partitions the dataset across nodes.
distractors: Replication and sharding both mean deleting all but one copy of the dataset.
Sharding always stores the complete dataset on every node.
Replication means each node stores a disjoint partition only.

System Design.fact: Consistent hashing maps keys and nodes onto a hash space so adding or removing a node remaps only a portion of keys rather than most of them.
System Design.correct_answer: Consistent hashing limits the fraction of keys that move when nodes join or leave.
distractors: Consistent hashing guarantees no key ever moves when membership changes.
Consistent hashing requires every key to be stored on every node.
Consistent hashing is a transaction isolation level.

System Design.fact: An idempotency key lets a server recognize retries of the same logical operation and avoid applying the side effect multiple times.
System Design.correct_answer: An idempotency key helps retries avoid duplicating the same side effect.
distractors: An idempotency key forces every retry to create a second side effect.
An idempotency key is used only to compress network packets.
An idempotency key replaces authentication credentials.
